request.spec:
When a grade has no rate in force on a date on a sheet nor on its parents, a sheet that was
cloned uses the rate of the sheet it was cloned from (and so on up that sheet's parents and
source).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
When a grade has no rate in force on a date on a sheet nor on its parents, a sheet that was
cloned uses the rate of the sheet it was cloned from (and so on up that sheet's parents and
source).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've made the change, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests: the new clone-source test and the three existing rate scenarios.

A cloned sheet now remembers which sheet it was cloned from. When a grade has no rate on a date on the sheet or its parents, the rate comes from that source sheet, then the source's parents, then the source's own source, and so on. The test checks that the lookup reads the source's rates as they are now, not a copy taken at clone time: a rate set on the source after the clone is picked up.

- **Stored data:** a new migration `V97__sheet_source.sql` adds a `sheet_source` table, and `Clones.copy` writes one row to it on each clone.
- **Server:** `Rates.lineage` builds the fallback order: the parents (still up to three levels), then the source and its own parents and source. Both the rate lookup behind each due and the inherited-rates endpoint now use it. A sheet is never visited twice, so a loop of sources can't make it run forever.
- **As-of view:** `AsOf` now also copies the source sheets' rates and settings when it rebuilds a sheet for a past date, so the as-of view falls back the same way.
- **Front end:** no logic change, because the screen already goes through the inherited levels in order. I only updated the comments in `useRates.ts`.

Only a sheet's own source is followed. If a parent sheet was itself cloned, its source is not used. That is my reading of the request, which only covers the cloned sheet and its source.
